method: Conservative analytic bounds for a finite source sphere and full divergent cone; all azimuths and continuous allowed focus range.

checks.note: Coaxial ring and pupil; optical head translates on +Y; fixed nominal LED axes; patch enclosed by sphere.

checks.continuousIntervalProof: Minimum focus is worst case; separation increases and inflated pupil angular radius decreases as the pupil moves upward.

checks.note: Upper end is the worst case before the crossover; whole finite-source beam stays outside the tube.
Every sample point is inside every nominal source-point cone. This establishes coverage, not uniform intensity or coverage by every point of the finite emitting patch.
Rigid transformation preserves these distances and angles only if lamps, sample, entrance and optical head share the tilt rig. Actual glTF hierarchy is a separate check.

limitations: Author-created dimensions; no manufacturer reconstruction or physical calibration.
Simulated entrance is a geometric acceptance proxy, not a measured optical entrance pupil or numerical aperture.
No gemstone refraction, multiple scattering, diffraction, stereo imaging, magnification, depth of field or radiometric calibration is calculated.
Direct geometric beam checks do not certify real stray-light suppression, internal reflections, LED lens performance, thermal safety or manufacturability.
Actual mesh clearances, control behavior and browser output require separate verification.

sources.use: Principle only: unscattered oblique illumination must miss the objective; some light redirected by the specimen can be collected.
Teaching context: brightfield and darkfield reveal different features; dust and surface scratches may also scatter light.
